# Text Field

> A single-line text field built on the native input, validation and all.

`<slab-text-field>` · Form · built on `<input>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/text-field/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/text-field.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-text-field
  label="Email"
  name="email"
  type="email"
  required
></slab-text-field>
```

`selectionStart`, `selectionEnd`, `selectionDirection`, `select()`, `setSelectionRange()` and `setRangeText()` work as they do on a native input, for things like a toolbar that wraps the selected text. Like a native input's, `setRangeText()` dispatches no "input" or "change". An email field has no selection, as an email input has none: the properties are `null`, and setting them, `setSelectionRange()` and `setRangeText()` throw.

## Elements

### `<slab-text-field>`

Import `slab-elements/text-field.js` to register it.

A single-line text field with no visual styles, around a native input, so it is typed into, focused, and read the way one is.

The label and the input are both in the shadow root, so a plain `for` reference names it without crossing out of one. The host delegates focus, so clicking anywhere on it, or a `<label for>` pointing at it, focuses the input.

Validity is the native input's. `required`, `minlength`, `maxlength`, `pattern` and `type` are passed through to it, and whatever it decides is mirrored onto the host, so `valueMissing`, `tooShort`, `patternMismatch` and `typeMismatch` all mean what they mean on an `<input>`. Nothing is computed twice.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(disabled)`, `:state(error)`, `:state(readonly)` and `:state(required)`. Where the label sits relative to the input is layout, so it's left to the styles around it.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type                                                            | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`                                                        |          | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                            |
| `autocomplete`     | `HTMLInputElement['autocomplete']`                              |          | What the browser may fill it with, as a native input's `autocomplete` says.                                                                              |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                                                       | `false`  | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                            |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean`                                                       | `false`  | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                         |
| `maxlength`        | `number`                                                        |          | The most characters the user can type, as a native input's `maxlength`.                                                                                  |
| `minlength`        | `number`                                                        |          | The fewest characters a valid value has, as a native input's `minlength`.                                                                                |
| `name`             | `string`                                                        | `''`     | The name its value is submitted under, as a native control's `name`.                                                                                     |
| `pattern`          | `string`                                                        |          | A regular expression a valid value matches, as a native input's `pattern`.                                                                               |
| `placeholder`      | `string`                                                        |          | Shown while it's empty, as a native input's `placeholder`. It's a hint, not a label.                                                                     |
| `readonly`         | `boolean`                                                       | `false`  | Lets the user select the value but not change it, as `readonly` does a native input. The value is still submitted.                                       |
| `required`         | `boolean`                                                       | `false`  | Makes it invalid while it has no value, as `required` does a native control.                                                                             |
| `type`             | `'text' \| 'email' \| 'password' \| 'search' \| 'tel' \| 'url'` | `'text'` | One of "text", "email", "password", "search", "tel" or "url". Number, date and time have components of their own.                                        |
| `value`            | `string`                                                        | `''`     | Like a native input, the attribute is the default value and the property is the current one, so the attribute doesn't change as the field is typed into. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultValue`                  | `string`                                 | The value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is, so setting it sets the attribute, and `value` with it.                                  |
| `selectionDirection`            | `HTMLInputElement['selectionDirection']` | Which way the selection was made, "forward", "backward" or "none", as a native input's `selectionDirection` is. `null` for an email field, which has no selection, as an email input's is, and setting it then throws.      |
| `selectionEnd`                  | `number \| null`                         | Where the selection ends, or where the caret is when nothing is selected, as a native input's `selectionEnd` is. `null` for an email field, which has no selection, as an email input's is, and setting it then throws.     |
| `selectionStart`                | `number \| null`                         | Where the selection starts, or where the caret is when nothing is selected, as a native input's `selectionStart` is. `null` for an email field, which has no selection, as an email input's is, and setting it then throws. |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null`                | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                                 | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`, or else the browser's own. Empty while it's valid.                                                            |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`                          | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                                | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                                                                           |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                                                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                                                             | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `click(): void`                                                                                        | Clicks it, as a native element's `click()` does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                                                                  | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                                                            | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                                                        | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `select(): void`                                                                                       | Selects its text, as a native input's `select()` does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                                                             | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `setRangeText(replacement: string, start?: number, end?: number, selectionMode?: SelectionMode): void` | Replaces part of its text, or the selection when `start` and `end` are left out, as a native input's `setRangeText()` does. `selectionMode` says what's selected afterward: "select", "start", "end" or "preserve", the default. Like a native input's, it dispatches no "input" or "change". Throws for an email field, as an email input does. |
| `setSelectionRange(start: number, end: number, direction?: 'forward' \| 'backward' \| 'none'): void`   | Selects part of its text, as a native input's `setSelectionRange()` does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void`                                      | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.               |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.             |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown. |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description` | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | Text about the field, and its validity message when it has one |
| `input`            | The input                                                      |
| `label`            | The label                                                      |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid      |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(error)`    | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
| `:state(readonly)` | While it's read-only.                                                                                                     |
| `:state(required)` | While it's required, for styles such as an asterisk.                                                                      |
